evidence: Receiving DO2 48.2h: 2.93 mg/L, falling monotonically to 1.73 mg/L at 52.0h — below minimum_do_mg_l of 2.0
Healthy receiving DO2 ~10.7-11.9 mg/L during 40-48h prior to the excursion
Delayed product assay: P = 1.08 g/L @36h, 3.05 g/L @48h — active production at risk of oxygen limitation
Source batches under similar trajectories maintained DO2 ≥ ~7.4 mg/L (e.g. source-3 74.8h), showing receiving-specific oxygen deficit
Allowed action bounds: combined = [0.8 feed, 1.15 air]
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~11 mg/L to 1.73 mg/L (48-52h), already violating the 2.0 mg/L oxygen floor, while product formation is still active (P 3.05 g/L @48h). A combined bounded intervention (feed ×0.8, air ×1.15) simultaneously reduces oxygen uptake demand and increases transfer capacity, giving the fastest return above the DO2 constraint while retaining product mass. Increase_air alone may recover too slowly given the demand trend; feed reductions alone sacrifice production; stop yields zero production.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters (kLa, OUR kinetics) are unknown, so the recovery rate under combined action is uncertain; DO2 could remain near 2 mg/L for several hours. If the DO2 deficit is driven by an unmodeled factor (e.g., a feed-composition or contamination issue rather than the O2 balance), reducing feed may not fully restore DO2. Residual risk that product quality/yield is modestly affected by temporary feed reduction.
